Recent observations from June 16 showed a maximum of 71°F under similar suppression, and forecasts for the 17th indicated no significant shift—such as stronger offshore winds or marine-layer erosion—that would push readings into the mid-70s or higher. Realistic challenges to this outcome remain limited but include an unexpected late-day clearing of the marine layer that could add a degree or two of insolation-driven warming, or minor revisions in the final official daily summary. High humidity and weak steering flow favor localized afternoon convection and thundershowers, which can reduce insolation and cap temperatures below radiative potential during peak heating hours. Minor differences among leading outcomes hinge on exact timing and coverage of cloud build-up or precipitation, as even modest increases in convective inhibition or boundary-layer mixing can shift the observed high by 1–2°C. Historical June maxima often reach 30–33°C, but basin topography and monsoon moisture introduce forecast spread that keeps probabilities distributed across the narrow band. Updated model runs and satellite observations of upstream moisture will provide the next key signals before resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent numerical weather prediction consensus from European and global models places Warsaw’s June 19 maximum between 27–29 °C under partly sunny skies and light northwesterly flow. Mid-June solar insolation supports rapid morning warming, yet modest cloud cover and a weak trough could limit the peak to 27 °C, while clearer conditions or stronger southerly advection favor 28–29 °C. The near-even split between 27 °C and 28 °C market shares reflects this narrow uncertainty band, as small shifts in boundary-layer mixing or afternoon convection timing routinely alter the daily high by 1 °C. Final high-resolution runs tonight will narrow the range ahead of official station observations.
